What makes Spinosaurus so amazing?

With a large sail on its back, the Spinosaurus is a special dinosaur that may have swum in the water. It's also considered one of the largest meat-eating dinosaurs ever known.

content.alt: Spinosaurus - Nature and science facts about Spinosaurus
content.text:
Nature and science facts about Spinosaurus

Research suggests that Spinosaurus's bones were denser and heavier than other dinosaurs', helping it adapt to life in the water, and its tail was broad like a paddle, well suited for swimming. The tip of its snout even had pores that sensed water pressure, like a crocodile's. The huge sail on its back (over 1.5 m tall) — the tallest spinal spines of any dinosaur — was more likely used for display than for controlling body temperature.

Points worth exploring together

Point out details like the back sail (display), the long snout (catching fish), the paddle-like tail (swimming), and the heavy bones (adaptation to water). It's fun to talk about it together: "Isn't it amazing that a dinosaur could swim?"

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Did Spinosaurus swim?
A. Research suggests it adapted to life in the water with heavy bones and a paddle-like tail. It's still being debated among scientists, though.

Q. What was the sail on its back used for?
A. It was more likely for visual display than for controlling body temperature. It had the tallest spinal spines of any dinosaur.

Q. How can we enjoy this at home?
A. Compare its snout and back with other meat-eating dinosaurs, and look for what it has in common with a crocodile.
